facts.text: Aluminium foil sheet on a pole, deployed on the lunar surface facing the Sun on 20 July 1969
facts.source: NASA Lunar Surface Journal & Apollo 11 Preliminary Science Report

facts.text: The Sun blows out a continuous stream of charged particles known as the solar wind
Earth's atmosphere and magnetic field deflect solar wind particles, but the airless Moon allows direct collection
Solar wind ions strike the foil and become embedded in its metallic surface layer
Exposed for 77 minutes on Tranquility Base, then rolled up, placed in a Teflon bag, and returned to Earth
Laboratory mass spectrometry measured helium-3, helium-4, neon, and argon, revealing the isotopic composition of the Sun
facts.source: University of Bern / Geiss et al., Science (1969)

scenes.kids: This is me, the Solar Wind Composition Experiment. A sheet of foil on a pole, standing on the Moon in 1969.
scenes.explorer: Solar Wind Composition Experiment, Apollo 11: an aluminium foil sheet on a pole, deployed on the lunar surface on 20 July 1969.

scenes.kids: My job is simple: face the Sun and catch what it throws at us.
scenes.explorer: Its design is simple: a thin foil sheet held up and turned toward the Sun.

scenes.kids: The Sun blows out tiny invisible bits all the time. That is the solar wind. On Earth, air and our magnetic field block it. The Moon has no air, so it reaches me.
scenes.explorer: The solar wind is a stream of charged particles from the Sun. Earth's atmosphere and magnetic field deflect it; on the airless Moon it reaches the surface.

scenes.kids: The bits crash into my foil and get stuck.
scenes.explorer: Solar wind ions strike the foil and become trapped in its surface.

scenes.kids: After 77 minutes, I am rolled up and carried home to Earth.
scenes.explorer: After 77 minutes of exposure, the foil is rolled up and returned to Earth.

scenes.kids: Scientists found helium, neon and argon trapped in me. That is how we learned what the Sun is made of.
scenes.explorer: Laboratory analysis measured helium-3, helium-4, neon and argon in the foil: the first direct measurement of solar wind composition from the lunar surface.
